Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The ants’ motions can be simulated event by event:

* **Collision 1 (A & B)** occurs at  
  \[
  t_1=\frac{30}{4}=7.5\text{ s},\qquad x=32.5\text{ cm}.
  \]  
  After this both reverse direction: A now moves left at \(3\) cm/s, B right at \(1\) cm/s.

* From that moment the next earliest events are simultaneous:
  * Ant A reaches the left end after another \(\Delta t_A=65/6\) s (total time \(t_2=t_1+\Delta t_A=55/3\approx18.33\) s).
  * At exactly that same moment ant B and ant C meet at  
    \[
    x_{BC}=130/3\text{ cm}\;(≈43.33\text{ cm}).
    \]

* After the B–C collision both reverse direction again: now B moves left (speed 1) from \(x=130/3\) and C moves right (speed 2).  
  * Ant B reaches the left end after a further  
    \[
    t_B=\frac{130/3}{1}=130/3\text{ s}.
    \]

Hence the last ant falls off at  

\[
T_{\text{last}}=t_2+t_B=\frac{55}{3}+\frac{130}{3}=\frac{185}{3}\text{ seconds}.
\]

This is exactly \(61\frac{2}{3}\) seconds (≈ 61.67 s).

ANSWER: 185/3
